findings.reason: Its proof invokes the empirical-fractions lemma, which requires within-group IID observed times and deterministic sample sizes tending to infinity. The Statement gives allocation fractions but omits those conditions; dependent repeated observations can violate the conclusion.

The sequential claim needs a filtration so past increments are measurable at later histories, a nonempty event risk set or zero-risk conventions (E_j is undefined when Y_j=0), and integrability such as bounded weights or finite sum E[w_j^2 V_j]. H-measurability alone does not ensure these.
The assignment-model supplier allows arbitrary finite assignment sets, but the logrank score is defined only for binary group maps z:I→{0,1}. Require each allowed assignment to induce such a map.

The stated censoring marginals and within-subject event/censoring independence do not determine the joint censoring law; dependence can make the claimed sample pattern have probability zero. Specify independence of censoring times across subjects and from event times, or state its joint probability.

The product-limit curve values use the Kaplan–Meier product formula, but the item neither states it nor declares its supplier. State the formula and show the calculation locally; the existing estimator definition gives the required factors.

The cited corollary applies under a full-record sharp null. Fixed observed event times do not state that each subject's record is unchanged across all allowed assignments; add that schedule assumption.
